summary:
**EarthTrend AI – An Earth System Trend and Multi-Hazard Intelligence Platform**

EarthTrend AI is an intelligent data analytics platform designed to explore historical natural disasters and identify patterns in multi-hazard activity. The system integrates selected datasets from NOAA, USGS and IBTrACS to analyse floods, tornadoes, landslides and tropical cyclones. It uses data ingestion, preprocessing, geospatial visualisation, statistical trend analysis and anomaly detection to transform historical records into meaningful insights. Through an interactive dashboard featuring a rotating 3D Earth, multi-hazard maps, graphical visualisations and analytical reports, users can explore disaster distributions, examine historical trends and identify unusual activity. Developed as a proof of concept using limited historical datasets, EarthTrend AI demonstrates how data analytics and geospatial technologies can support better understanding of natural hazards, with future scope for expanded global coverage and advanced predictive capabilities.
details:
Project Details – EarthTrend AI

EarthTrend AI is a prototype of an Earth System Trend and Multi-Hazard Intelligence Platform developed to analyse historical natural disaster data and identify meaningful patterns. The project integrates selected datasets from NOAA, USGS and IBTrACS, covering floods, tornadoes, landslides and tropical cyclones. It includes data ingestion, preprocessing, statistical trend analysis, anomaly detection, geospatial visualisation and an interactive Streamlit dashboard with a 3D rotating globe. The system helps users explore historical disaster records, understand geographic distributions and identify unusual patterns in disaster activity. However, EarthTrend AI is currently a partially developed proof of concept and not a complete or fully operational disaster monitoring and prediction system. It uses limited historical datasets and requires further development, including wider geographical coverage, additional data sources, improved analytical models and advanced predictive capabilities. The project demonstrates the potential of combining artificial intelligence, data analytics and geospatial technologies to support better understanding of natural hazards.
